facts.text: On this date in 1620, the Mayflower departed Plymouth, England — carrying 102 passengers, fewer people than fit in a standard Boeing 737.
On this date in 1975, Papua New Guinea gained independence, becoming the world's most linguistically dense nation: 800+ languages spoken across a population smaller than London's.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires per capita than any country on Earth — roughly one in three residents qualifies — yet it maintains a fully professional army of 82 soldiers.
The Philippines is the only country in Asia where the majority of the population is Christian, a legacy of 333 years of Spanish colonial rule that ended in 1898.
Tokyo's greater metropolitan area houses 37 million people — more than the entire population of Canada — yet its murder rate is lower than that of Boise, Idaho.
On this date in 1992, George Soros broke the Bank of England. His fund shorted £10 billion in sterling, forcing the UK out of the ERM and netting him roughly $1 billion in a single day.
Black Wednesday — September 16, 1992 — cost the British Treasury an estimated £3.3 billion. The pound's humiliation ultimately accelerated Britain's drift away from European monetary union.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792. The 24 brokers who signed the agreement set the commission rate at 0.25% — a cartel arrangement that held, more or less, for 200 years.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway originally made textiles. He later called buying it the worst investment of his life, estimating the opportunity cost at roughly $200 billion.
The entire global bond market — around $140 trillion — is larger than the stock market and the world's GDP combined, yet it receives a fraction of the financial news coverage equities do.

On this date in 1848, a tamping iron blasted through Phineas Gage's skull, destroying his frontal lobe. He survived, but his personality inverted so completely that friends said he was 'no longer Gage.'
On this date in 1965, the Surveyor program confirmed the Moon's surface could support a lander's weight — until then, some scientists genuinely feared spacecraft would sink into deep lunar dust.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces most of its atoms every few years, yet the pattern persists. You are less a thing than a self-sustaining wave moving through matter.

Quantum entanglement has been demonstrated across 1,200 kilometers. Two particles share a fate instantaneously, with no signal passing between them — a fact Einstein called 'spooky action at a distance' and never accepted.
On this day in 1620, the Mayflower departed Plymouth for America — a ship smaller than a modern McDonald's restaurant, carrying 102 people across 3,000 miles of open Atlantic.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Medieval Europe had tenure disputes before Tenochtitlán had walls.
On this day in 1810, Mexico declared independence — a nation that would outlast the Ottoman Empire, the British Raj, and the Soviet Union, all of which seemed far more permanent.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient Egypt was already ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before the American Civil War began. Japan was still faxing government documents in 2021.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast that dictionaries treat it as naturalized.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable by design — the language built a word for homesickness with nowhere to go.
On this date in 1620, the Mayflower departed Plymouth, England. The ship's name was utterly ordinary — 'mayflower' was common slang for the hawthorn blossom, not a grand christening.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language has fewer than a handful of living speakers; the word outlives them.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of a used bookstore, also from Koenig's Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows. That one man named so many unnamed feelings says something about how many were waiting.
On this date in 2017, China's central bank ordered all domestic cryptocurrency exchanges to shut down by Sept 30 — Bitcoin dropped 30% within days, then tripled by December.

On Sept 16, 2021, OpenSea disclosed that a former employee had used insider knowledge to front-run featured NFT listings — the first major NFT insider-trading case, later prosecuted under wire fraud statutes.
Bitcoin's whitepaper never uses the word 'blockchain' — Satoshi called it a 'chain of blocks', and the compound noun entered common usage years later through the broader developer community.
The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum itself — it exploited a reentrancy flaw in The DAO's own Solidity code, a distinction Ethereum's core developers used to justify the hard fork.

Ethereum validators can be slashed for signing two conflicting blocks in the same slot — the penalty starts small but scales with how many validators misbehave simultaneously, punishing coordinated attacks far more than accidents.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published the Transformer paper. Every major language model today — GPT, Gemini, Claude — descends directly from that eight-author, 12-page document.
On this date in 2019, OpenAI released GPT-2 in staged increments, citing misuse risk. The model they deemed too dangerous has since been dwarfed roughly 1,500-fold in parameter count.
AlphaFold 2 predicted protein structures for virtually every known organism — around 200 million proteins — in under a year. Experimental biology would have taken centuries to match that output.
Training GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed more electricity than 1,000 U.S. homes use in a year. Inference — running the model for users — likely costs more in total energy than training did.
The first neural network to defeat a human Go champion, AlphaGo, learned the game by playing itself 4.9 million times in 72 hours — a volume of experience no human could accumulate in a lifetime.
